segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsections 3 and 4,
a driver
shall not drive on the left side of the highway within such zone or drive across or on the left side of any pavement striping designed to mark such zone throughout its length.
A driver may drive across a pavement striping marking such zone
to an adjoining highway if the driver has first given the appropriate turn signal
and there will be no impediment to
oncoming or following traffic.
Except where otherwise provided,
a driver may drive across a pavement striping marking such a zone
to make a left-hand turn
if the driver has first given the appropriate turn signal
in compliance with NRS 484B.413 [NRS-484B-413-2],
if it is safe
and if it would not be an impediment to
oncoming or following traffic.

elements.justification: DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'driver' means 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle'. The driver is a relational role, not membership (ru.aggregate: 'Not a stand-in for: a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle'), so the role is read through the controlled motion of the vehicle (observable_reading agency) and the binder is the vehicle, 'true when the user carries an included class' of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the same mapping the index records for 'the driver' (LVMC_11_16_030).

(i) The left side of the highway is the side to the left of the line dividing its two directions: st.centre_line, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', tied to the highway the subject occupies by st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') and rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') on st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines'; we read the way, not the roadway, so its exclusion does not apply). Being on the left side is read with prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', against half the body's width from kin.extent ('a formula reads the full length, width and height'): the body is on the left side where the line's offset is below half the width by more than p.lateral_position_tolerance. Same reading as the index's 'must not be driven to the left side of the highway' (NRS_484B_213_2a). (ii) 'Such zone' is the no-passing zone the section's first subsection lets an authority indicate 'by appropriate signs or markings'. A sign: dev.zone_sign, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {..., no_passing, ...}; end attribute', with dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', on a st.travel_region the subject occupies (rel.occupies); the sign read is a beginning sign (end false); its 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now' does not apply since no legend condition is read. A marking: st.lane_marking, 'per side of a lane: type ∈ {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}, colour ∈ {white, yellow, other}', on the left side of the st.lane the subject occupies: a solid or double_solid yellow line marks the zone for that lane; a solid_broken line, whose solid half the atom does not place, leaves membership unknown. The zone's presence on the road is the evidence of its designation (status). (iii) The pavement striping designed to mark the zone is the no-passing marking of s4 (st.lane_marking type solid or double_solid, colour yellow, on the left side of the subject's lane), which on a two-way highway lies along st.centre_line ('the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions'). Driving across it or on its left side is the body reaching past that line: prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line ('left positive') below half the width from kin.extent less p.lateral_position_tolerance. 'Throughout its length' is read by judging every observation at which the subject is in the zone.

The permitted act is the same crossing the obligation forbids (s5): the vehicle's body reaching past the zone's centre-line striping, prim.region_lateral_offset ('left positive') against half the kin.extent width; 'A driver' is the vehicle, as in s2.

'To an adjoining highway' states where the crossing leads, a purpose read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading purpose): within p.vehicle_turn_window ahead the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') other than the highway h of the zone and no longer occupies h. 'Has first given the appropriate turn signal': sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}', showing left, or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {..., left, ...}', meaning left, at the last observation before the crossing began (the crossing having held at every observation since). The indicator's 'Not a stand-in for: the turn or lane change itself' does not apply: the signal is read, not the manoeuvre.

The same crossing as s6 (prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line against half the kin.extent width) by the vehicle. The region at which the left-hand turn of s11 is declared is the place a left turn leaves the highway for: st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet') or st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'); the declared intention takes one of them as its target.

'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'. Oncoming: rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing', with tolerance p.oncoming_heading_cos; its exclusion (not the direction a road user approaches an intersection from) does not apply, as the words concern road users meeting the subject head-on on this highway. Following: a member behind the subject, 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for ... immediately to the rear)' (rel.bearing, negative longitudinal component), with 'headings aligned' (rel.same_direction, tolerance p.contest_same_direction_cos).

As s8b: members of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic that are oncoming (rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing') or following (behind by rel.bearing, 'immediately to the rear', with rel.same_direction, 'headings aligned').

The appropriate signal for a crossing to the left to make a left-hand turn is sig.turn_indicator state left or sig.hand_signal meaning left ('a driver's or rider's arm signal'), given at the last observation before the crossing began; its manner and distance are the compliance with NRS 484B.413 composed on s13. Not the turn itself (indicator's exclusion).

operationalizations.standard: no impediment to oncoming or following traffic
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a road user of traffic is impeded where its centre and the subject's, under constant velocities, approach within the conflict horizon to a centre distance below the conflict clearance; oncoming is rel.oncoming within the opposed-heading tolerance, following is a road user behind the subject (negative longitudinal bearing) with headings aligned within the same-direction tolerance; read at every observation of the crossing

traffic-conflict technique: the crossing is safe where no road user of the scene is in contact with the subject and none approaches the subject's centre, under constant velocities, within the conflict horizon to a centre distance below the conflict clearance; read at every observation of the crossing

operationalizations.standard: no impediment to oncoming or following traffic
operationalizations.convention: as for s8: traffic-conflict technique on oncoming (rel.oncoming) and following (behind, headings aligned) members of traffic, read at every observation of the crossing

residues.why: 'Except where otherwise provided' defers to provisions it does not name; those provisions are judged by their own rules, and this rule's verdict on crossing the striping to make a left-hand turn is the same whether or not they apply.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a highway h on which a centre line c lies, and is within a no-passing zone: it occupies a travel region that a dev.zone_sign of kind no_passing (end false) governs, or it occupies a lane whose left-side st.lane_marking is solid or double_solid and yellow (where that marking is solid_broken, membership is unknown).
obligation: At every such observation the subject's body does not reach past the centre line c to its left: the lateral offset of c from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset, left positive) is not below half the subject's width (kin.extent) minus p.lateral_position_tolerance. A crossing is excused (E3) where, within p.vehicle_turn_window ahead, the subject occupies a highway other than h and no longer occupies h; at the last observation before the crossing began (the crossing having held at every observation since) its turn indicator showed left or its hand signal meant left; and at every observation of the crossing no member of traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) that is oncoming (rel.oncoming, p.oncoming_heading_cos) or following (behind by rel.bearing, rel.same_direction within p.contest_same_direction_cos) has a closest approach to the subject within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. A crossing is also excused (E4) where the subject's declared intention int.left_turn at an intersection or a driveway/alley entrance holds at the observation; the left signal was given as in E3; NRS_484B_413_2 is complied with for the subject; no road user is in contact with the subject or has such a closest approach (safe); and no oncoming or following member of traffic has such a closest approach (impediment).

narrowings.why: 'a driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it

The striping designed to mark the zone is read where it lies along the centre line dividing the two directions; a no-passing marking between two lanes of the same direction is not read as the zone's striping.
'to an adjoining highway' is read through the conduct it explains: the subject reaching another highway within the turn window after the crossing
'impediment' is read only through closest-approach conflicts with oncoming or following road users of traffic; a slowing of traffic without such a conflict is not read
'impediment' is read only through closest-approach conflicts with oncoming or following road users of traffic

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle occupies a lane whose left st.lane_marking is solid yellow; it moves left until prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line is -1.0 m to overtake a slower vehicle; int.left_turn is declared false at every region and it stays on the same highway.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the same no-passing lane (left marking solid yellow) and keeps the centre line 0.9 m to its left with a body width of 1.8 m plus margin: the offset stays above half its width minus the tolerance.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject's lane has a broken white left marking and no no_passing dev.zone_sign governs any region it occupies; it crosses the centre line to overtake.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source does not observe st.lane_marking and no zone sign is in the scene; the subject's body reaches past the centre line.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: In the no-passing zone the subject's int.left_turn is declared true at a driveway_or_alley_entrance; its left indicator has been on for the last 120 m and NRS_484B_413_2 is complied with; it crosses the centre line; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1 but sig.turn_indicator is off and sig.hand_signal no_signal at the observation before the crossing.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1 but an oncoming vehicle (rel.oncoming) has a closest approach to the subject in 2 s at a centre distance of 1 m.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1 but the left indicator came on only 10 m before the crossing, so NRS_484B_413_2 is violated although a signal was given at the observation before the crossing.

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: In the zone the subject signals left, crosses the centre line and within the turn window occupies another highway and no longer the zone's highway; no oncoming or following road user has a conflicting closest approach.

param_proposals.name: p.lateral_position_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the lateral margin within which a vehicle body counts as at a line or an edge: lane-keeping variability of a driven vehicle plus the source's position error
param_proposals.source: naturalistic lane-keeping studies; source position error

param_proposals.name: p.vehicle_turn_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of a turn by a motor vehicle at a junction or into or out of a driveway, from the start of its heading change to its end, including the crossing of opposing lanes
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance (left-turn time gap 7.5 s) plus a margin

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions

param_proposals.name: p.contest_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 18 degrees) for travel in the same direction

segmentation.text: Upon a highway designated and signposted for one-way traffic
a vehicle
shall be driven only in the direction designated.

elements.justification: st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction', occupied by the subject (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'), as the index maps 'Upon any highway on which traffic is restricted to one direction of movement' (NRS_484B_210_1). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel', whose direction the designation restricts. 'Designated and signposted' is legal status: the one-way roadway's presence on the road is its evidence (observable_reading status).

'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

'Only in the direction designated' forbids motion against the one-way roadway's designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — ... a roadway, one-way roadway'): drv.motion.moving_against_carrier(subject, r) on the one-way roadway r of s1, with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'Driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a one-way roadway r (st.one_way_roadway).
obligation: At every such observation, for every one-way roadway r the subject occupies, the subject is not moving against r's designated direction: drv.motion.moving_against_carrier(subject, r) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance does not hold.

narrowings.why: 'designated and signposted' is read through the one-way roadway's presence on the road, the evidence of its designation and posting
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it

'only in the direction designated' is read as no motion component against the designated direction beyond the speed resolution; motion across the roadway (entering or leaving it) is not read as a breach

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a st.one_way_roadway whose st.lane_direction is (1,0) and moves with kin.velocity (-8,0) m/s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the same one-way roadway and moves with kin.velocity (8,0) m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a two-way st.roadway (not a one-way roadway) and moves in either direction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a one-way roadway whose st.lane_direction the source does not supply, moving at 8 m/s.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution

contract: Road user a moves against the designated direction of travel of carrier region r: part of its motion runs opposite to r's designated direction. It is observed as the component of a's velocity (kin.velocity) along r's designated direction (st.lane_direction), the dot product of the velocity with the direction as a formula reads it normalised, being below minus speed_tol: the part of a's motion that runs against r's direction exceeds the speed the source cannot tell from rest. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of where a's body points, of the gear selected, of how long a has moved so, or of why. Not denoted: a road user at rest; one whose velocity component against r's direction is at or below speed_tol, such as one moving along r's direction or straight across it. Where r carries no designated direction, or a's velocity is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed component at or below which motion against the direction counts as none: the source's speed resolution

elements.justification: kin.velocity: 'velocity vector', m/s, world frame; its component along the direction is a dot product.
st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in', read normalised by a formula; a place no carrier covers has none (unknown).

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: r's st.lane_direction is (1,0); a's kin.velocity is (-5,0) m/s; the component -5 m/s is below minus speed_tol.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: r's st.lane_direction is (1,0); a's kin.velocity is (5,0.2) m/s; the component is positive.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: a's kin.velocity is not observed.

segmentation.text: A vehicle
passing around a rotary traffic island
shall be driven only to the right of such island.

elements.justification: 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

A rotary traffic island is st.roundabout, 'a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches'; passing around it is the subject's footprint overlapping that region (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'), the same mapping the index gives 'within a roundabout' (LVMC_11_43_010_A). 'Traffic' here names the island, a structure, not road users the duty turns on, so the traffic aggregate is not claimed.

Passing with the island on the vehicle's left, i.e. to the right of it, is travel counter-clockwise about the island's centre seen from above; driving to its left is travel clockwise about it: drv.motion.circulating_clockwise_about(subject, r), 'the point lies to the right of a's direction of travel and a's velocity turns about it clockwise', on the roundabout r of s2, with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance and sin_tol = p.roundabout_clockwise_sin_tol, must not hold. Same concept the index maps for 'shall be in a counterclockwise direction' (LVMC_11_43_010_A).

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a roundabout region r (st.roundabout).
obligation: At every such observation, for every roundabout r the subject occupies, drv.motion.circulating_clockwise_about(subject, r) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance and sin_tol = p.roundabout_clockwise_sin_tol does not hold.

narrowings.why: 'to the right of such island' is read as not travelling clockwise about the roundabout's reference point, taken as the centre of its central island; motion towards or away from the centre (entry, exit) is not a breach
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a st.roundabout whose reference point is at (0,0); at kin.position (0,-15) it moves with kin.velocity (-6,0) m/s: the centre is on its right and it turns clockwise.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: At kin.position (0,-15) in the roundabout the subject moves with kin.velocity (6,0) m/s: counter-clockwise, island on its left.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies no roundabout; it drives on a straight roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the roundabout but its kin.velocity is not observed.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution

param_proposals.name: p.roundabout_clockwise_sin_tol
param_proposals.convention: the share of a vehicle's speed across the line to the roundabout's centre at or below which its motion counts as towards or away from the centre rather than around it: within about 15 degrees of the radial direction

segmentation.text: If a highway has two or more clearly marked lanes for traffic traveling in one direction,
vehicles must:
Not be moved from that lane until the driver has given the appropriate turn signal
and ascertained that such movement can be made with safety.

elements.justification: The subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles', and st.lane_adjacency gives 'the count of lanes in that direction', which is at least the literal two. Same mapping as the index's 'which has two or more clearly marked lanes for traveling in the same direction' (NRS_484B_208_1). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic whose direction the lanes serve. 'Clearly marked' is the lanes' presence on the road (observable_reading status); lane_adjacency's 'Not a stand-in for: the marking between two lanes' does not apply, since the count of lanes is what is read.
'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

A move from that lane is the subject, occupying the lane l1 of s1, coming to overlap its neighbouring lane of the same direction: drv.lane.entering_adjacent_lane(subject, l1, l2, side), read at the observation at which it holds, with side left or right. The appropriate signal is the one for the side of the move: sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}', showing that side, or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {..., left, right, ...}', meaning it; 'until ... has given' places it before the move: at the observation of the move and at the one before it. The indicator's exclusion (not the lane change itself) does not apply: the signal is read beside the move.

operationalizations.standard: such movement can be made with safety
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: at the observation the move begins, no other road user is in contact with the subject and none approaches the subject's centre, under constant velocities, within the conflict horizon to a centre distance below the conflict clearance

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a lane l1 whose direction has at least two lanes (st.lane_adjacency count, literal 2), and at the observation it begins to move into the neighbouring lane l2 of the same direction on side s (drv.lane.entering_adjacent_lane(subject, l1, l2, s), s left or right).
obligation: At that observation and at the observation before it, the subject's turn indicator shows s or its hand signal means s; and at that observation no other road user is in contact with the subject (rel.contact) or has a closest approach to it within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'clearly marked' is read through the lanes' presence on the road
'the appropriate turn signal' is read as the indicator or arm signal of the side of the move, shown at the move and at the observation before it; its duration is not read here
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled conduct
'ascertained' is read through the outcome it secures: the movement made without a conflict

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a carriageway with two lanes in its direction the subject, in the right lane, comes to overlap the left lane while sig.turn_indicator is off and sig.hand_signal no_signal.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject's left indicator is on for 3 s before and during its move into the left lane; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a lane whose direction has one lane (st.lane_adjacency count 1) and keeps to it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves into the left neighbouring lane; sig.turn_indicator is not observed and sig.hand_signal reads no_signal; no other road user.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject signals left and moves into the left lane while a faster vehicle there has a closest approach to it in 1 s at a centre distance of 1 m.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width

contract: Road user a, occupying lane r1, begins to move into lane r2, the neighbouring lane of the same direction on side s of r1 (s left or right): the event of a's footprint first reaching into r2 from r1. It is observed with a's footprint occupancy (rel.occupies) and the lanes' adjacency (st.lane_adjacency): r2 is r1's neighbour on side s, a's footprint overlaps both r1 and r2 at the observation, and at the previous observation it overlapped r1 and did not overlap r2. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until a's footprint has ceased to overlap r2 and again comes to overlap it from r1. It says nothing of whether a completes the move, of its signal, of its speed, or of why it moves. Not denoted: a road user that comes into r2 from elsewhere than r1; one that stays within r1; a lane r2 that is not r1's neighbour of the same direction on side s, such as an opposing lane. Where a's overlap with either lane at the observation or at the previous one is unobserved, or the adjacency of the two lanes is not observed, it is unknown.

elements.justification: rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'.
st.lane_adjacency: 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction'; its exclusion (not the marking between two lanes) does not apply.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: r2 is r1's left neighbour; a overlapped r1 only at the previous observation and overlaps r1 and r2 now; s is left.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: a overlaps r1 only at both observations.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: a overlaps r1 and r2 now, but its overlap with r2 at the previous observation is unobserved.

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single center lane to be used only for turning by traffic moving in both directions,
the following rules apply:
A vehicle
may be driven in the center turn lane
only for the purpose of making a left-hand turn
onto or from the highway.

elements.justification: st.centre_turn_lane: 'a single centre lane used only for turning by traffic in both directions', the words' own configuration; 'center' (DEF-NRS-484A-040) places it on the line that indicates 'each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions'. The subject occupies it (rel.occupies). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic whose turns the lane serves. 'Designed to provide' is the lane's presence on the road (observable_reading status).
'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.
Driven in the centre turn lane: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the st.centre_turn_lane of s1.

'From the highway': the declared intention of s5 is taken at the place a left turn leaves the highway for, st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet') or st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'). 'Onto the highway': the left turn already made into the lane, read through conduct (observable_reading purpose): the subject has occupied the centre turn lane c at every observation since drv.motion.left_turn ('has completed a turn to the left') was recognized while it occupied c, and at some observation of the turn window behind that recognition it occupied no part of the highway h (st.highway) on which c lies (st.on_way, 'the public way a structure region lies on').

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a centre turn lane c (st.centre_turn_lane).
obligation: At every such observation the subject's presence in c is excused, and otherwise violated, where either (from) the subject's declared intention int.left_turn at some intersection or driveway/alley entrance region holds at that observation, or (onto) the subject has occupied c at every observation since an observation at which drv.motion.left_turn(subject) (window = p.vehicle_turn_window, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol = p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) held while it occupied c, and at some observation of the window p.vehicle_turn_window behind that observation it occupied no part of the highway h on which c lies.

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'designed to provide' is read through the centre turn lane's presence on the road
a left-hand turn onto the highway is read through the turn the subject made into the lane from off the highway, which explains its presence there

scenarios.name: forbid

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single center lane to be used only for turning by traffic moving in both directions,
the following rules apply:
A vehicle
must not travel more than 200 feet in a center turn lane
before making a left-hand turn from the highway.

elements.justification: st.centre_turn_lane: 'a single centre lane used only for turning by traffic in both directions'; 'center' (DEF-NRS-484A-040) places it on the line that indicates 'each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions'. Occupied by the subject (rel.occupies). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. 'Designed to provide' is the lane's presence (status).
'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

The travel in the lane is the distance the subject travelled while its footprint continuously overlapped (rel.occupies) the st.centre_turn_lane c, a distance along its path (kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path'), written with Term.distanceWhile; it is compared with the literal 200 ft.

The left-hand turn is drv.motion.left_turn, 'has completed a turn to the left', recognized at the observation its heading change settles; it is a turn from the highway made out of the centre turn lane: the subject occupied c (rel.occupies) at some observation of the turn window behind the recognition and no longer occupies c at it. The travel limit is read at the last observation of that window at which it occupied c.

applicability: drv.motion.left_turn(subject) (window = p.vehicle_turn_window, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol = p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) holds at the observation, and for a centre turn lane c the subject occupied c at some observation of the window p.vehicle_turn_window behind and does not occupy c at this observation.
obligation: At the last observation of that window at which the subject occupied c, the path length over which it had occupied c continuously (Term.distanceWhile subject (rel.occupies subject c)) is at most the literal 200 ft. Where that run in c began before the recording the distance is unknown.

narrowings.why: the travel limited is the continuous run in the centre turn lane ending at the left turn; a run before an earlier exit from the lane is not added
'travel' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single center lane to be used only for turning by traffic moving in both directions,
the following rules apply:
A vehicle
must not travel more than 50 feet in a center turn lane
after making a left-hand turn onto the highway
before merging with traffic.

elements.justification: st.centre_turn_lane: 'a single centre lane used only for turning by traffic in both directions'; 'center' (DEF-NRS-484A-040) places it on the line that indicates 'each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions'. Occupied by the subject (rel.occupies). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. 'Designed to provide' is the lane's presence (status).
'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

The travel in the lane after the turn is the distance along the subject's path (kin.path_length) over which it has stayed in the st.centre_turn_lane c (rel.occupies) since the turn, written with Term.distanceWhile; compared with the literal 50 ft.

The left-hand turn is drv.motion.left_turn, 'has completed a turn to the left', recognized while the subject occupies c; it is a turn onto the highway where, at some observation of the turn window behind the recognition, the subject occupied (rel.occupies) no part of the st.highway h on which c lies (st.on_way, 'the public way a structure region lies on'): it came from a driveway or another way.

Merging with traffic (the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic travelling in the through lanes) ends the counted travel: the subject's footprint ceases to overlap (rel.occupies) the centre turn lane c.

applicability: For a centre turn lane c lying on a highway h: the subject has occupied c at every observation since an observation at which drv.motion.left_turn(subject) (window = p.vehicle_turn_window, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol = p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) held while it occupied c, and at some observation of the window p.vehicle_turn_window behind that observation it occupied no part of h.
obligation: The path length over which that condition has held (Term.distanceWhile subject of it) is at most the literal 50 ft. The count ends when the subject's footprint leaves c (merging).

narrowings.why: the merge is read as complete when the footprint leaves the centre turn lane; distance travelled while straddling c and a through lane counts
'travel' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning,
a vehicle must:
Be driven in the right turn lane
only for the purpose of making a right turn.

elements.justification: st.turn_lane: 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}', with side right, occupied by the subject (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). 'Designed to provide' is the lane's presence on the road (observable_reading status).
'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

Driven in the right turn lane: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the st.turn_lane of side right. The right turn the lane serves is made at st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet') or at st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'): the declared intention of s4 takes one of them as its target region.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the right at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a turn lane t of side right (st.turn_lane).
obligation: At every such observation the subject's declared intention int.right_turn holds at some intersection or driveway/alley entrance region; where it is false at every such region the subject's presence in t is violated, and where it is undeclared it is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'designed to provide' is read through the right turn lane's presence on the road
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
